newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Mystery liquid causes scare at HK handover site.
newsitem.headline: Mystery liquid causes scare at HK handover site.

text.p: Cleaners put Hong Kong police on alert after leaving tins of an unidentified liquid near the site where Britain's Prince Charles will hand over the territory to Chinese President Jiang Zemin later on Monday.
Smoke billowed out after police opened five of seven tins they found late on Sunday night beside a flower bed near the heavily guarded Convention Centre, police said on Monday.
A government chemist summoned to the scene quickly put a name to the smoking liquid -- hydrochloric acid.
Police said they believe the acid, used for cleaning, had been left behind by workers at the Convention Centre.
More than 4,000 VIPs are due to crowd into the Grand Hall to witness the ceremony at midnight (1600 GMT) marking the British territory's reversion to Chinese rule.
